summary_1line: King Parikshit insults a silent sage by placing a dead snake on him; the sage’s son Sringin angrily curses the king to die by serpent Takshaka.

image_candidates.scene_text: The weary king Parikshit lifts a dead snake with the tip of his bow and drapes it across the silent sage’s shoulders in the forest cow-pen.
Young ascetic Sringin, eyes blazing with anger, touches water and pronounces a curse that the serpent king Takshaka will kill Parikshit in seven nights.
The meditating sage sits unmoving in a rustic cow-pen, calves drinking milk nearby while a dead snake lies across his shoulders.
